dervis-irab:1-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غُثاءً) In the Qāmūs: "al-ghuthāʾ, like ghurāb and like zinnār: rubbish, foam, and the perished, worn-out leaves of trees." It also says: "al-qamsh is the plural of qumāsh, which is the scraps of things on the face of the earth, so that the dregs of people are called qumāsh, and 'he gave me nothing but qumāsh', i.e. the poorest thing he found." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "ghuthāʾ al-sayl is what the flood carries; ghathā al-wādī, ghuthūwan (of the pattern qaʿada), means the valley became full of ghuthāʾ; and ghathat nafsuhu, taghthā, ghathyan (of the pattern ramā) and ghathayānan is its turbulence, so that one is nearly sick, from a mixture flowing into the mouth of the stomach."
(أَحْوى) al-aḥwā is of the pattern afʿal from al-ḥuwwa, which is a blackness tending to greenness; it is also said that al-aḥwā is greenness with blackness upon it; al-aḥwā is also the gazelle, because it has two lines on its back; one says "a man aḥwā" and "a woman ḥawwāʾ", and its plural is ḥuwwun, like aḥmar and ḥumr. In the Qāmūs: "al-ḥuwwa, with ḍamma, is blackness toward greenness, or redness toward blackness; ḥawiya, like raḍiya, ḥawan." Ibn Jinnī said: al-ḥuwwa is a redness tending to blackness that occurs in the lip, and the Arabs find that desirable. Dhū l-Rumma said:
لمياء في شفتيها حوّة لعس ... وفي اللّثات وفي أنيابها شنب
صفراء في نعج بيضاء في دعج ... كأنها فضة قد مسّها ذهب
(A slender-lipped girl, in whose lips is a dark ruddiness, a deep red, and in her gums and in her teeth a cool sweetness; yellow-tinged in her fair whiteness, white against the dark of her eyes, as if she were silver that gold has touched.)
And Abū ʿUbayda recited, also from Dhū l-Rumma, about the pasture that is aḥwā:
حوّاء قرحاء أشراطيّة وكفت ... فيها الذهاب وحفتها البراعيم
(A dark-green, white-blazed pasture of the Ashrāṭ star, on which the light rains dripped, and the buds surrounded it.)
al-qarḥāʾ is the white one; one says "qarḥa" of a blaze (ghurra); ashrāṭiyya means rained on by the star-setting of the two Sharaṭān; al-dhihāb, with kasra on the dhāl, is light rain; and al-barāʿīm is the plural of burʿūma, which is the flower before it opens, and it is also called the kamm, the plural being aknām.

* I'rab:
(سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى) سبّح is an imperative verb, meaning "declare transcendent", and has been treated before; its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; and اسم ربك is its direct object. Al-Jalāl made it an interpolated word, on the model of Labīd's saying:
إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما ... ومن يبك حولا كاملا فقد اعتذر
(Until the year, then the name of peace be upon you both; and whoever weeps a full year has made his excuse.)
There is no need for this strained reading, since declaring transcendent may fall upon the name, i.e. declare the name of your Lord transcendent above being used to name an idol or image, so that it is called "lord" or "god". And الأعلى is an adjective of ربك; Ibn Hishām allowed it to be an adjective of اسم. (الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى) الذي is a second adjective of the Lord; the clause خلق is the ṣila (relative clause), and the object of خلق is omitted, i.e. "everything"; the فاء is a conjunction, and سوّى is conjoined to خلق. What is meant by "proportioning" is that He created what He willed in the most complete and perfect manner, according to an order described as firm and masterly, free of blemishes and defects. (وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدى) This too is conjoined, in sequence, to what preceded. (وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعى فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أَحْوى)
This too is conjoined to what precedes it; the clause أخرج is the ṣila of الذي, and المرعى is the direct object; فجعله is conjoined to أخرج, the هاء is the first direct object, غثاء is the second direct object, and أحوى is an adjective of غثاء. But a difficulty arises, since al-ghuthāʾ is the dry matter while al-ḥuwwa is a lasting greenness, so the two contradict each other. It is therefore preferable to parse أحوى as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from المرعى, i.e. "He brought it forth aḥwā, black from the intensity of greenness, and then made it ghuthāʾ after its ḥuwwa." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that أحوى is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought it out of the pasture black from the intensity of greenness and abundant watering, and then made it ghuthāʾ after its ḥuwwa." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As for His saying, the Exalted, أحوى, it is said that it is an adjective of غثاء, and it is said that it is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought forth the pasture green and then turned it into ghuthāʾ, so he put part of the ṣila first." Abū Ḥayyān said: "The apparent sense is that أحوى is an adjective of غثاء. Ibn ʿAbbās said the meaning is: He made it dark ghuthāʾ, i.e. black, because when ghuthāʾ ages and rain strikes it, it blackens and rots and becomes aḥwā. It is also said that أحوى is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought forth the pasture aḥwā, i.e. black from the intensity of its greenness and freshness through abundant watering; and the postposing of أحوى is good for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil). He said:
وغيث من الوسمي حوّ تلاعه ... تبطنته بشيظم صلّتان
(And a rain from the wasmī season, whose hollows are dark-green, I entered it on a long-legged, lean, swift horse.)"
Ibn Khālawayh said in his book "I'rab of Thirty Surahs of the Noble Qur'an": "فجعله غثاء أحوى means that Allah made the pasture aḥwā, and al-aḥwā is intensely green, tending to black because of abundant watering, and then He turned it into ghuthāʾ after it dried; so the meaning involves a fronting and postponing." Ibn Hishām said in his book al-Mughnī, in mentioning the aspects from which an objection may enter against the one who parses: "The fourteenth is the saying of some about أحوى that it is an adjective of غثاء. This is not correct without qualification; it is so only if aḥwā is interpreted as black from dryness and withering. But if it is interpreted as black from the intensity of greenness through abundant watering, as مُدْهَامَّتَانِ was interpreted, then making it an adjective of غثاء is like making قيما an adjective of عوجا; rather it must be a ḥāl from المرعى, postposed to match the verse-endings." By my life, he has settled the dispute in what he laid down. (سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى) The سين is a particle of futurity; نقرئك is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the كاف is a direct object; the فاء is a conjunction; لا is negative; and تنسى is an imperfect verb, nominative. The wording of Abū l-Suʿūd: "سنقرئك فلا تنسى is an exposition of Allah the Exalted's special guidance of His Messenger ﷺ following the exposition of His general guidance of all His creatures, namely his, peace be upon him, guidance to receive the revelation, to memorize the Qur'an, and his guidance of all people. The سين is either for emphasis or because what is meant is making him recite what Allah revealed to him at that time and what would be revealed to him afterwards, so it is a promise that the revelation will continue within the promise of making him recite, i.e. We shall make you recite what We reveal to you, and what follows, through the tongue of Jibrīl, or We shall make you a reciter by inspiring recitation, so you will not forget at all, from the firmness of memorization and mastery, even though you are unlettered, not knowing what writing or reading is; so that is another sign for you, besides what lies within what you recite of the clear signs, in respect of inimitability and of informing about the unseen." The فاء is a conjunction and لا is negative: Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet that he would not forget. تنسى is an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative sign being the implied ḍamma on the alif. It is also said that لا is prohibitive and تنسى is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its jussive sign being the dropping of the weak letter, and then the alif was brought as a support for the fatḥa of the sīn so as to agree with the verse-endings, as in His saying السبيلا. Abū Ḥayyān did well when he condemned this view; he said: "This is a weak statement; the sense of the verse is utterly clear, and they have been far-fetched in understanding it." (إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ وَما يَخْفى) إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is the object of تنسى; the exception is vacated (mufarragh) from the most general of objects; the clause شاء الله is the ṣila of ما; and the clause إن and what is within its scope is a justification of what precedes; إن and its noun; the clause يعلم is its predicate; and الجهر is a direct object;
the واو is a conjunction and ما is a relative noun conjoined to الجهر; the clause يخفى is its ṣila. Al-Samīn said: "It is not permissible for it to be maṣdar-forming, lest the verb be left without an agent; were it not for that, its being maṣdar-forming would be better, so that an interpreted maṣdar would be conjoined to a plain maṣdar like it." (وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرى فَذَكِّرْ إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرى) The واو is a conjunction; ونيسرك is conjoined to سنقرئك; it is an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the كاف is a direct object; and ولليسرى are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to نيسرك, i.e. to the tolerant Islamic law. The فاء is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you know that you are among those who receive perfecting outpourings through Our guidance and success, then remind"; إن is conditional; نفعت is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); and الذكرى is the agent. In إن there is a sense of regarding it as improbable, as though he were sure they would not incline to guidance and would persist in riding the back of excess. The apodosis (jawāb) of إن is omitted, indicated by what precedes. Al-Zamakhsharī has a subtle question and a subtler answer. He said: "If you say: the Messenger ﷺ was commanded to remind whether the reminder benefits or not, so what is the meaning of making benefit a condition? I say: it has two aspects. One is that the Messenger of Allah had already exhausted his effort in reminding them, and they only increased in insolence and tyranny from the increase of reminding, and the Prophet ﷺ was burning with regret and anguish and increasing in grief and eagerness over reminding them; so it was said to him: 'You are not a compeller over them' — so remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My threat, and turn away from them and say 'Peace', and remind if the reminder benefits, and that is after the argument has been established by repeated reminding. The second is that it is conditional in form, but its meaning is a censure of those who remind, a report of their state, a regarding as improbable that the reminder will affect them, and a recording against them that their hearts are sealed, as you say to the preacher, 'Enrage the tax-collectors, if they listen to you,' intending by this condition to regard that as improbable and that it will never be." As for Ibn Khālawayh, after citing the view we cited he said: "Others say: إن means قد, i.e. remind, for the reminder has benefited; but that is very remote, and supposition and speculation do not befit the style of the Qur'an." As for Abū Ḥayyān, he said:
"The apparent sense is that his command to remind is conditional on the reminder's benefit, and this condition was brought only as a rebuke to Quraysh, i.e. if the reminder benefits these tyrannical, obstinate ones, and its meaning is the improbability of their benefiting from the reminder. It is as the poet said:
لقد أسمعت لو ناديت حيّا ... ولكن لا حياة لمن تنادي
(You have made yourself heard, had you called one alive; but there is no life in him whom you call.)
Al-Farrāʾ, al-Naḥḥās, al-Zahrāwī and al-Jurjānī said: its meaning is 'and if it does not benefit', so he limited himself to the one alternative because it indicates the other." (سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشى، وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى، الَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرى، ثُمَّ لا يَمُوتُ فِيها وَلا يَحْيى) The سين is a particle of futurity; يذكر is an imperfect verb, nominative; من is a relative noun, the agent; the clause يخشى is a ṣila with no grammatical position; ويتجنبها is conjoined to سيذكّر; the هاء is a direct object and the pronoun refers back to الذكرى; and الأشقى is the agent. Ibn Khālawayh said: "One says 'Zayd is al-ashqā' and 'the woman is al-shaqyā', like al-aʿlā and al-ʿulyā, and one says: 'al-ashqā spoke to al-shaqyā', 'the two ashqayn spoke to the two shaqyayn', 'the ashqūn spoke to the ashqayn', and 'the shaqiyyāt spoke to the shaqiyyāt'." الذي is an adjective of الأشقى; the clause يصلّى has no position because it is the ṣila of الذي; the agent of يصلّى is a latent pronoun referring to الأشقى; النار is a direct object and الكبرى is an adjective of النار; ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; لا is negative; يموت is an imperfect verb, nominative; وفيها are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to يموت; and ولا يحيا is conjoined to لا يموت. The meaning of the delay is that wavering between life and death is more terrible than burning, so it is delayed from it in degrees of severity: "he who dies is at rest"; but these are neither dead, that they might rest, nor alive, that they might find a breath from the punishment. (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى) قد is a particle of affirmation; أفلح is a past verb; من is the agent; the clause تزكى, i.e. purified himself, has no position because it is the ṣila of من; وذكر is conjoined to تزكى; واسم ربه is a direct object; and فصلّى is conjoined to ذكر. (بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقى) It is an iḍrāb (turning away) from an implied statement to which the speech leads, the implied form being: "you do not do what is for the good of your affair, rather you prefer"; تؤثرون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the واو is the agent; الحياة is a direct object and الدنيا is an adjective of الحياة. What is meant by preferring the life of this world is inclining to it, being deceived by its adornments, and seeking out its milk-flows. The واو is a ḥāl-wāw; الآخرة is a mubtadaʾ (subject); خير is the khabar (predicate); and أبقى is conjoined to خير; so in it are the pleasures of this world and what the mind cannot conceive of increase upon them, and it has besides that the attribute of permanence and eternity. (إِنَّ هذا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولى صُحُفِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى) إن is a particle resembling the verb; هذا is its noun, the demonstrative referring to the success of him who purified himself and the words that followed; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); في الصحف is the predicate of إن; الأولى is an adjective of الصحف; and صحف إبراهيم وموسى is a badal (substitute) for الصحف.

* Benefits:
A glimpse of the scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā:
In al-Khāzin the following is reported: From Abū Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The mosque has a greeting." I said: "And what is its greeting, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Two rakʿas that you pray." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, has Allah revealed to you anything of what was in the scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā?" He said: "O Abū Dharr, recite: قد أفلح من تزكّى وذكر اسم ربه فصلّى بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا والآخرة خير وأبقى إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Mūsā?" He said: "They were all lessons: 'I wonder at one who is certain of death, how he can rejoice; I wonder at one who is certain of the Fire, how he can laugh; I wonder at one who sees the world and how it turns with its people, how he can feel at ease with it; I wonder at one who is certain of destiny, and then is angry; I wonder at one who is certain of the reckoning, and then does not act.'"
In al-Qurṭubī the following is reported: "Al-Ājurrī narrated from Abū Dharr, who said: I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Ibrāhīm?' He said: 'They were all parables: O king, empowered, tried, deluded: I did not send you to heap up the world one part upon another, but I sent you to repel from Me the plea of the wronged, for I do not reject it, even were it from the mouth of an unbeliever.' And in them were parables: 'It is for the wise person to have an hour in which he converses privately with his Lord, an hour in which he reflects on the handiwork of Allah, mighty and majestic, and an hour in which he is alone for his needs of food and drink. And it is for the wise person to covet only three things: provision for the return, a means for livelihood, and a pleasure in what is not forbidden. And it is for the wise person to be discerning of his time, attending to his own affair, guarding his tongue; and whoever counts his speech as part of his deeds, his speech is little except in what concerns him.'"
